The interest rate for debentures issued under these other provisions with respect to a loan or mortgage committed or endorsed during the 6-month period beginning July 1, 2026, is 5 percent.

items.summary: The Section 184 Indian Housing Loan Guarantee Program ("Section 184 Program") operates using a combination of funds annually appropriated by Congress and fees. Consistent with other HUD loan guarantee programs, to ensure that the program is self-sustaining, HUD is increasing fees charged under the program. HUD is increasing the upfront loan guarantee fee for all new Section 184 Firm Commitments, including refinances, from 1.00 to 1.50 percent, effective October 1, 2026. HUD is increasing the upfront loan guarantee fee for all new Section 184 Skilled Workers Demonstration Program Firm Commitments, from 0 to 1.00 percent, effective October 1, 2026. The Annual Loan Guarantee Fee will remain at zero for all Section 184 loans.

feature_pitch_raw:
**The pattern:** Next year's Social Security arithmetic became public today. The Federal Register notice of 10/26/26, "Cost-of-Living Increase and Other Determinations for 2027," sets a 3.6 percent cost-of-living increase in benefits effective December 2026 and fixes the national average wage index for 2025 at $72,800.33, a figure the notice says drives other program parameters. Read it against the BLS medical care Consumer Price Index for September 2026 — 593.65 on the 1982-84=100 scale, up 1.5 percent year over year — and the raise is more than double the measured rise in medical prices. Justice in Aging listed the 2027 COLA as still pending in its 10/16/26 Washington roundup; as of this morning the number exists, and no monitored publisher has matched it.

**Why it matters:** The increase takes effect in December 2026, so the check that lands then is the one readers will budget against for the whole of 2027. For once a benefit adjustment is running ahead of the medical price series most often used to argue it is not: 3.6 percent against 1.5 percent. Whether that headroom survives contact with the rest of the notice is the open question, because the same document re-prices other program parameters off the $72,800.33 wage index, and nothing in the record says a beneficiary has been told which of those apply to them.

**Why pitch this now:** The increase is effective December 2026, five weeks out, and the notice published 10/26/26 — the newest item in this run at zero days old. This is also the window when people set 2027 budgets and finish Medicare decisions, and it is a confirmed gap: the monitored publishers cover this beat and none has it.

**Angle:** Whether a 3.6 percent raise actually gains ground for an older household, given that medical care prices rose 1.5 percent in the year to September 2026 and the same notice resets parameters most beneficiaries never see. Working title: "What 3.6 Percent Actually Buys in 2027." For readers within a decade of, or already drawing, Social Security.

**Potential headlines:**
- Social Security benefits rise 3.6 percent starting in December
- Your raise beats medical inflation this year, 3.6 percent against 1.5
- The $72,800.33 wage figure that quietly sets your 2027 Social Security numbers

**Potential outlets:**
- **Kiplinger** — retirement economics is the house specialty, and a COLA-versus-medical-CPI comparison with the wage index explained is exactly the service piece its readers plan their year around.
- **Bankrate Retirement** — publishes consumer finance data stories on Social Security and Medicare and can carry the arithmetic down to a monthly-dollar level.
